g.text: assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "The server passed validation with MCPJam CLI 6.2.2.\n\n- **Config:** `/workspace
/mcp.json` has no credential, and the server returns 401 without one. I passed `MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` as a bearer token on the command
line instead.\n- **Probe and validate:** Both succeeded. The server is `arithmetic-fixture` 1.0.0, protocol 2025-11-25, over stre
amable HTTP with no OAuth. It advertises only the `tools` capability.\n- **Doctor:** The report status is `ready`. The only noise
was warnings about resources, which the server doesn't advertise. The full report is in `doctor.json`.\n- **Tools:** The server ha
s one tool, `add`, with an input and output schema. `add(2,3)` returned `{\"sum\":5}`. `add(\"x\")` returned `isError: true` with
the message \"a and b must be finite numbers\", which is the right behavior for bad input.\n- **Not done:** I didn't run the accou
nt-side `mcpjam cloud` commands, so nothing was checked against `MCPJAM_API_URL` or project_fixture.\n- **Saved work:** `/workspac
e/validate.sh` reruns these checks (it needs `MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` set).\n\n**Concern note:** I expected `mcp.json` to carry the auth
, and it doesn't. Add a header or token entry there if other tools need to read that file. Nothing blocked me, and I didn't need t
he account owner or any other human action."}], "container": null, "stop_reason": null, "stop_sequence": null, "stop_details": nul
